Containers, grouping and missing values

Source: vignettes/containers-and-missing-values.Rmd
containers-and-missing-values.Rmd

This guide explains the types of objects tidystata returns, how groups and missing values affect calculations, and how to preview a table without changing its data. Start with Getting started for a short workflow.

Container types and lists 

library(tidystata)
library(dplyr)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'dplyr'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union

df <- data.frame(
  group = c("A", "A", "B", NA),
  answer = c("yes", NA, "no", "yes"),
  score = c(2, NA, 6, 8)
)
tbl <- tibble::as_tibble(df)

class(tab(df, answer))
#> [1] "data.frame"
class(tab(tbl, answer))
#> [1] "tbl_df"     "tbl"        "data.frame"
class(summ(df, score))
#> [1] "data.frame"
class(summ(tbl, score))
#> [1] "tbl_df"     "tbl"        "data.frame"

New tables from the tab, summ, codebook and variables families preserve a base data frame, tibble or data.table input. A list result remains a list, and each table inside follows the same rule. An explicit output option takes precedence. pwcorr(), misstable() and duplicates_report() are exceptions: they always return tibbles.

base_tables <- tab1(df, answer, group)
class(base_tables)
#> [1] "list"
class(base_tables$answer)
#> [1] "data.frame"
class(fre(df, answer, .type = "tibble"))
#> [1] "tbl_df"     "tbl"        "data.frame"

Other data-frame subclasses are not reconstructed on newly shaped tables. Vectors, such as the result of ds() or row_mean(), keep their intentional vector output. New data.table summaries do not retain input keys or indexes.

data.table inputs follow the same rule:

if (requireNamespace("data.table", quietly = TRUE)) {
  dt <- data.table::as.data.table(df)
  class(tab(dt, answer))
  class(summ(dt, score))
}
#> [1] "data.table" "data.frame"

For a formatted table, install flextable and request .type = "flextable":

if (requireNamespace("flextable", quietly = TRUE)) {
  rich <- fre(tbl, answer, .type = "flextable")
  class(rich)
}
#> [1] "flextable"

Grouping and denominators 

grouped <- group_by(tbl, group)
tab(grouped, answer)
#> # A tibble: 4 x 7
#>   group answer     n percent   cum valid valid_cum
#>   <chr> <chr>  <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 A     yes        1      50    50   100       100
#> 2 A     NA         1      50   100    NA        NA
#> 3 B     no         1     100   100   100       100
#> 4 NA    yes        1     100   100   100       100
summary <- summ(grouped, score, .stat = c("n", "mean", "missing"))
summary
#> # A tibble: 3 x 5
#>   group type      n  mean missing
#>   <chr> <chr> <int> <dbl>   <int>
#> 1 A     dbl       1     2       1
#> 2 B     dbl       1     6       0
#> 3 NA    dbl       1     8       0
group_vars(summary)
#> character(0)

Summary and inventory results are ungrouped. Grouping keys remain ordinary columns where reported. For tab(), tab1(), fre(), fre1(), summ() and tabstat(), .by = NULL inherits existing groups; an explicit .by replaces them. tab2() and fre2() require explicit .by for grouped cross-tabulations; otherwise, they tabulate the whole input regardless of existing groups.

summ(grouped, score, .by = answer, .stat = c("n", "mean"))
#> # A tibble: 3 x 4
#>   answer type      n  mean
#>   <chr>  <chr> <int> <dbl>
#> 1 no     dbl       1     6
#> 2 yes    dbl       2     5
#> 3 NA     dbl       0    NA

Cross-tabulation with tab2() or fre2() returns one table per group, in a list named after each group:

crossed <- tab2(df, answer, score, .by = group)
names(crossed)
#> [1] "group = A"  "group = B"  "group = NA"

One-way tabulations use all observations within a group for percent and cum, on a zero-to-100 scale. valid and valid_cum exclude missing measured values. Missing grouping keys are ordinary groups. In summaries, valid_pct is instead a fraction from zero to one. summ(.missing = FALSE) removes missing grouping keys; numeric calculations always omit missing measured values.

tab(tbl, answer)
#> # A tibble: 3 x 6
#>   answer     n percent   cum valid valid_cum
#>   <chr>  <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 no         1      25    25  33.3      33.3
#> 2 yes        2      50    75  66.7     100  
#> 3 NA         1      25   100  NA        NA
summ(tbl, score, .stat = c("n", "miss_n", "valid_pct", "mean"))
#> # A tibble: 1 x 5
#>   type      n miss_n valid_pct  mean
#>   <chr> <int>  <int>     <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 dbl       3      1      0.75  5.33
summ(tbl, score, .by = group, .missing = FALSE, .stat = c("n", "mean"))
#> # A tibble: 2 x 4
#>   group type      n  mean
#>   <chr> <chr> <int> <dbl>
#> 1 A     dbl       1     2
#> 2 B     dbl       1     6

Empty and all-missing measurements 

empty <- tbl[0, ]
summ(empty, score, .stat = c("n", "sum", "mean"))
#> # A tibble: 1 x 4
#>   type      n   sum  mean
#>   <chr> <int> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 dbl       0    NA    NA
tab1(tbl, starts_with("absent"))
#> named list()

missing <- tibble(a = c(NA_real_, NA_real_), b = c(NA_real_, 4))
summ(missing, a, .stat = c("n", "sum", "mean"))
#> Warning: a is entirely missing; retained with n = 0.
#> # A tibble: 1 x 4
#>   type      n   sum  mean
#>   <chr> <int> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 dbl       0    NA    NA
row_sum(missing)
#> [1] 0 4
row_mean(missing)
#> [1] NA  4

An ungrouped numeric column with no observations remains in a summary with n = 0 and NA statistics, including sum. An all-missing row instead has a row sum of zero and a row mean of NA. Empty selections give empty results for tabulation; row helpers require at least one column. Matrix columns are not supported by the tabulation and column-summary interfaces.

Labels and special missing values

Variable labels describe columns; value labels describe particular values. Numeric calculations exclude SPSS user-missing codes and Stata tagged missing values. Tabulations report missing categories alongside observed values.

labelled <- tibble(
  response = haven::labelled_spss(
    c(1, 2, 99, NA),
    labels = c(Yes = 1, No = 2, Refused = 99),
    na_values = 99,
    label = "Interview response"
  )
)
variables(labelled)
#> # A tibble: 1 x 2
#>   name     label             
#>   <chr>    <chr>             
#> 1 response Interview response
codebook(labelled)
#> # A tibble: 1 x 5
#>   variable label              type             n unique
#>   <chr>    <chr>              <chr>        <int>  <int>
#> 1 response Interview response double+label     2      2
tab(labelled, response)
#> # A tibble: 4 x 6
#>   response              n percent   cum valid valid_cum
#>   <dbl+lbl>         <int>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1  1 [Yes]              1      25    25    50        50
#> 2  2 [No]               1      25    50    50       100
#> 3 99 (NA) [Refused]     1      25    75    NA        NA
#> 4 NA                    1      25   100    NA        NA
decode(labelled$response)
#> [1] "Yes"     "No"      "Refused" NA

Summary statistics for labelled numeric measurements use their underlying values and exclude SPSS user-missing codes. Factors use level codes and warn; choose measurements deliberately instead of averaging category codes. decode() displays value labels when present, but does not itself recode every labelled refusal into an ordinary NA.

Numeric and calendar summary tables 

mixed <- tibble(score = c(2, 4), day = as.Date("2024-01-01") + c(0, 2))
separate <- summ(mixed, .stat = c("n", "min", "mean", "sd", "max"))
#> A list is returned as statistics are heterogeneous.
names(separate)
#> [1] "numeric" "date"
separate$numeric
#> # A tibble: 1 x 7
#>   name  type      n   min  mean    sd   max
#>   <chr> <chr> <int> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 score dbl       2     2     3  1.41     4
separate$date
#> # A tibble: 1 x 7
#>   name  type      n min        mean       sd            max       
#>   <chr> <chr> <int> <chr>      <chr>      <drtn>        <chr>     
#> 1 day   date      2 2024-01-01 2024-01-02 1.414214 days 2024-01-03
class(separate$date$sd)
#> [1] "difftime"
combined <- summ(mixed, .type = "table", .stat = c("n", "min", "mean", "sd", "max"))
combined
#> # A tibble: 2 x 7
#>   name  type            n min        mean          sd max       
#>   <chr> <chr>       <int> <chr>      <chr>      <dbl> <chr>     
#> 1 score dbl             2 2          3           1.41 4         
#> 2 day   date [days]     2 2024-01-01 2024-01-02  1.41 2024-01-03
class(combined$sd)
#> [1] "numeric"

Default list mode keeps numeric statistics numeric in their own table. Calendar locations such as min, mean and max are formatted dates or date-times, while a spread such as sd stays a difftime. Table mode combines families. A location column shared by numeric and calendar rows becomes character, and the spread column becomes a plain number of days for dates or seconds for date-times, with the unit shown in the type column.

SD uses the sample denominator. Percentiles use Stata’s rule; for example, the quartiles of 1:4 are 1.5 and 3.5. See summ() for formulas, weights and other statistics.

A preview retains every row 

long <- tibble(id = 1:12, value = (1:12)^2)
preview <- preview_table(long, n = 4)
preview
#> # A tibble: 12 x 2
#>       id value
#>    <int> <dbl>
#>  1     1     1
#>  2     2     4
#> 11    11   121
#> 12    12   144
#> # ... 8 rows omitted in the middle; use print(x, n = Inf) to show all rows.
nrow(preview)
#> [1] 12
sum(preview$value)
#> [1] 650

subset <- slice_headtail(long, n = 4)
subset
#> # A tibble: 4 x 2
#>      id value
#>   <int> <dbl>
#> 1     1     1
#> 2     2     4
#> 3    11   121
#> 4    12   144
nrow(subset)
#> [1] 4
sum(subset$value)
#> [1] 270

The preview still contains 12 rows; the slice contains four. n is the total display or selection budget, split between the beginning and end. Interval mode samples approximately evenly spaced positions; sort first when position should represent a meaningful order.

preview_table(long, style = "interval", n = 4)
#> # A tibble: 12 x 2
#>       id value
#>    <int> <dbl>
#>  1     1     1
#>  5     5    25
#>  8     8    64
#> 12    12   144
#> # ... 8 rows omitted between displayed positions; use print(x, n = Inf) to show
#> # all rows.
ordinary <- unpreview_table(preview)
identical(ordinary, long)
#> [1] TRUE

print_headtail() and print_interval() print once and invisibly return the complete input. unpreview_table() removes the persistent display setting. Supported dplyr/tidyr operations carry preview settings forward while following their own container and grouping rules. Wrapping and unwrapping a data.table copies it; later native data.table mutations retain ordinary reference semantics.
